---
name: project-board
description: Move GitHub issues between project board columns (Triage, Todo, Doing, Review, Testing, Done), order a column, set board fields (Priority, Size, Estimate, Start date, End date), edit blocked-by relationships and mark which agent works on an issue via the Agent issue field. Use when an issue-workflow agent (triager, coder, reviewer, tester) hands an issue over, claims it, or needs its board status.
---

# Project Board

`scripts/board.sh` does all board access for the workflow agents and `scripts/blockers.sh` all Relationship edits. Call them instead of writing `gh` commands yourself. They use GraphQL only and keep the API usage small: **one query reads everything, one request applies all changes**, so prefer one call with several issues or fields over many calls. Field and option ids are resolved at runtime, so any board made from `board-template` works.

## Commands

Run from inside the repo (or set `GH_REPO`). `<n>` is the issue number. Names are case-insensitive; the emoji in column names is not needed.

```bash
scripts/board.sh info <n>                          # board fields + current Agent
scripts/board.sh move <n> Doing                    # Triage | Todo | Doing | Review | Testing | Done; clears Agent
scripts/board.sh move <n> Todo Priority=P1 Size=M Estimate=6   # column + fields in one request
scripts/board.sh apply <<'PLAN'                    # many issues, different fields, ONE request; Status=... also clears Agent
4|Status=Todo|Priority=P0|Size=M|Estimate=6
5|Priority=P1|--if-empty
PLAN
scripts/board.sh set <n> Priority=P0 Size=XS       # Priority P0-P2, Size XS-XL, Estimate=<number>
scripts/board.sh move <n> Doing "Start date:=today"     # Field:=Value sets the field only when it is empty (dates: YYYY-MM-DD or today)
scripts/board.sh set <n> Priority=P1 --if-empty    # --if-empty does that for every field of the call
scripts/board.sh claim Coder <n> [<n>...]          # Triager | Coder | Reviewer | Tester
scripts/board.sh release <n> [<n>...]
scripts/board.sh order <n1> <n2> <n3>              # put the issues in this order (relative order within each column)
scripts/board.sh add <n>                           # put issue on the repo's linked board in Triage (kept if already on a board)
```

`add` is skipped when the repo has no linked board. `order` lists must contain issues of one board, each once; list all issues of a column you want ordered. In a plan, fields are separated by `|` and `--if-empty` applies to the whole line; never use it on a line that sets `Status` (the column would stay): use `Field:=Value` there.

## Relationships

`scripts/blockers.sh` reads and edits the native "blocked by" relationships (no board needed):

```bash
scripts/blockers.sh list <n>                  # what <n> is blocked by, with state and title
scripts/blockers.sh add <n> <blocker>...      # kept if it exists; a self-link or direct cycle is refused with an error (report it, do not retry)
scripts/blockers.sh remove <n> <blocker>...   # kept if it does not exist
```

## Hand-off pattern

1. When you pick an issue up: `claim` it (and `move` it to your column if needed).
2. When you finish: `move` it to the next column. `move` always clears the Agent field, so an empty Agent means nobody is working on it.
3. Set board fields when your role owns them: triager sets Priority, Size, Estimate; coder sets Start date on first Doing (`Start date:=today`, so rework keeps the original); tester sets End date on Done.

## Parking an issue for the user

`needs-info` means: no agent can go on without the user (missing information, a decision, a dispute, the review-round cap). An agent that gets there does not guess and does not leave the issue half-way in its column: it **parks** it in Triage, where the triager leaves `needs-info` issues alone. So Triage with `needs-info` is the one place that lists everything waiting for the user.

```bash
gh label create needs-info --force      # only if the label does not exist yet
gh issue edit <n> --add-label needs-info
gh issue comment <n> --body-file - <<'COMMENT'
> *This was generated by AI.*
<what is needed and why; for a dispute both positions>
COMMENT
scripts/board.sh move <n> Triage        # also clears the Agent field
```

The user answers in a comment and removes `needs-info`; then the issue either goes to its next column by hand or stays in Triage for the triager to queue. An open PR stays linked, so later rework continues on its branch. Technical failures (an API error, a refused push) are not parking reasons: stop, report, leave the issue where it is.

## No board

If the issue is on no project board, board commands print `SKIPPED: ...` and exit 0. This is not an error: do your own work, leave the issue where it is and post a short hand-off comment (what you did, which agent or step is next). The Agent field, relationships, branches, PRs and comments do not need a board and still work. `move` without a board skips the column but still clears Agent.

## Errors

API problems (including rate limits) are errors, never "no board"; the message carries the API's reason. All changes of one command go in one request and are applied in order; if the API rejects it, earlier changes of that request may already be applied, so re-run `info` before retrying.

- `issue field 'Agent' not found`: create the single-select field Agent (Triager, Coder, Reviewer, Tester) under Settings > Issue fields.
- A message about a missing scope: the user must run `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s <scope>` (`read:user` for the Agent field, `project` for the board).
- `option '...' not found`: the message lists the valid options.
